clue.text: Purposeful group argue about monarch getting jolly

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for arguing is read backwards

parts.note: to row is to argue noisily
a king is a monarch
a jolly is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A determined team bickers about a king who is enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW into WOR. Jolly is used as a noun, an outing or party.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee set up to investigate a particular issue is a group formed for a specific purpose.

clue.text: Old factory in an expression in legal document

indicators.note: in places the phrase for 'an expression' inside the legal document

parts.note: a will is a legal document
an gives A
a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: Someone finds a turn of phrase in a legal paper about an old works.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill driven by a water wheel is a historic kind of factory.

clue.text: Nick — name involved in downfall?

indicators.note: involved in places the abbreviation for name within the word for downfall

parts.note: ruin is downfall

explanation.surface: A theft whose name is tied up with someone's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is a verb in British slang, to arrest; a run-in is a brush with the law, so read Nick as a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang nick means an arrest, and a run-in with the police is such an encounter.

clue.text: Contribution of Russian PM the wrong way round

indicators.note: the wrong way round swaps the two halves of the leader's name, the back part going to the front

parts.note: Vladimir Putin was Russian Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A political input from the Russian premier, reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: PUT and IN swap places rather than every letter being reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An input is something one contributes, such as advice or effort.

clue.text: What was once fired to blow up ogre's path

indicators.note: to blow up means to explode, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A monster's route is to be exploded with explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was a cluster of small iron balls once fired from cannon.

clue.text: Woman needs added weight, beginning to read as radio broadcaster?

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

indicators.note: beginning to means take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A woman needs to gain weight before she starts to read on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is someone who presents on radio, introducing programmes.

clue.text: Time to defeat an unpleasant old woman?

parts.note: to rout is to defeat heavily

explanation.surface: It is time to see off a disagreeable elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old trout' is British slang for a bad-tempered older woman, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a disparaging colloquial term for an unpleasant older woman.

clue.text: Actor sprawled out in moorland barn

indicators.note: sprawled out means spread untidily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star lies stretched out in a barn on the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an American film star of On the Waterfront and The Godfather, so an actor by profession.

clue.text: Part of Birmingham little short of a gem

indicators.note: little short of means the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: a stone is a gem

explanation.surface: A Birmingham district is nearly as precious as a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston is a district of Birmingham, home of Aston Villa football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston is an inner-city area of Birmingham, England.

clue.text: Indulging in sport? Yen disappears when boy's into that church music

indicators.note: into places the boy within the shortened word
disappears means the yen symbol is removed from the word

parts.note: playing is indulging in sport
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
a son is a boy; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A complicated story of a game, money vanishing and a boy entering church.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing Y leaves PLAING, and SON goes in after PLAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval church chant.

clue.text: A restriction that's no problem for smashing women?

definitions.text: A restriction that's no problem for smashing women?

parts.words: A restriction that's no problem for smashing women?
parts.note: an invisible barrier to women's promotion, which 'smashing' women would break through, punning on smashing as excellent and as shattering

explanation.surface: A rule that excellent women find easy to break.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an unseen barrier stopping women reaching senior positions.

clue.text: Spectacles look right (gent changed them regularly)

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of gent are rearranged
regularly picks every other letter of the word them

explanation.surface: A gentleman alters his glasses periodically and they look right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns GENT into GNET; 'regularly' takes T and E from THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of glasses held up on a long handle, a kind of spectacles.

clue.text: Extremist from university left paintings around?

indicators.note: around means the word for paintings is turned backwards

parts.note: art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: A radical from college leaves pictures lying about.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, an extremist.

clue.text: Cleaner hurls a bin when upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleaner throws a rubbish bin around in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brush for scrubbing fingernails is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: To act smartly, criminal's beginning to get jemmy under crate

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the following pieces below the crate

parts.note: a box is a crate

indicators.note: beginning to selects the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a jemmy is a crowbar, a type of lever

explanation.surface: A crook starts using a crowbar on a crate to show some cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box clever' is British slang for acting shrewdly.
explanation.definitionFit: To box clever is a British idiom meaning to behave cleverly or cunningly.

clue.text: Awful-looking nude is upset and embarrassed, turning no one on?

indicators.note: awful-looking suggests the letters of nude are a mess, so they are rearranged
upset, in a down clue, turns the word is upside down

parts.note: red means flushed with embarrassment

explanation.surface: An unattractive naked figure blushes, having no appeal to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful-looking' makes UNDE of NUDE; 'upset' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that excites no one is not wanted, so unwanted.

clue.text: Cabinets for sick people?

explanation.definitionFit: Cases are both display cabinets and patients under medical care.

clue.text: Producer of silk print seen in special display

indicators.note: a special display suggests the letters are laid out in a new way

explanation.surface: A printed fabric is shown at a special exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ through which a spider or silkworm extrudes silk.

clue.text: King grabs the Parisian female to wind down

indicators.note: grabs means the king's word holds the article inside

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king
la is the feminine French word for the

explanation.surface: A monarch seizes a French woman to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax is to unwind and calm down.

clue.text: Resolve to prevent something exploding?

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: The aim is to stop a bomb going off.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to decide firmly, to resolve.

clue.text: Feature of church with Latin — something to gaze at?

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A church has Latin inscriptions worth staring at.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to navel-gazing, self-absorbed contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: Navel-gazing is the idiom for introspection, so the belly button is what one gazes at.

clue.text: Place of contest goddess finally changed

indicators.note: finally changed means the last letter of the goddess's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: A goddess finally alters the location of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of VENUS becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where a sporting event or contest is held.

clue.text: Poem brought into major match towards end of tournament?

indicators.note: brought into places the poem inside the word for major

parts.note: seminal means highly influential, major
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A poem is read out at a big game near the end of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major match' looks like one phrase, but major is wordplay and match begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is the round of matches just before the final of a tournament.

clue.text: Head of multinational employs nine inspiring females

indicators.note: head of selects the first letter of the next word

parts.note: uses means employs

explanation.surface: A company boss hires nine women.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were the nine goddesses in Greek myth who inspired the arts.

clue.text: Lie about bit of stuff

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A lie about some small item.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibre is a thread, a small piece of material.

clue.text: We take everything in!

parts.note: spoken by creatures that eat both plants and meat, taking all kinds of food into their bodies

explanation.definitionFit: Animals eating both plant and animal food consume everything.

clue.text: Poet Nancy must have stood here in the White House

parts.note: Nancy Reagan stood by her husband, so her place was beside him
Ron, Ronald Reagan, was the US president living in the White House

explanation.surface: A poet recalls where a First Lady stood at the President's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a celebrated English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Engineers attending offensive smell that's breaking out again

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army
crude means coarse and offensive
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Engineers notice a foul odour that is returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Recrudescent describes something, such as a disease, flaring up again after dormancy.
